title: k8s-helm-node-provisioning-debug-notes
content:
Quick scratchpad for debugging node provisioning failures with Helm + autoscaler/cloud-init. Capture commands tried, errors, hypotheses, and next steps.

Context:
- Staging cluster (AWS-like) with autoscaled nodegroups, kubelet v1.27.
- Symptom: new nodes show as NotReady or never join. node-bootstrap helm chart runs init containers + daemonset to finalize setup. Failures often after image pull TLS errors or CNI flaps.

Observed:
- Cloud instance running, kubelet present but node state NotReady (KubeletNotReady or NetworkUnavailable).
- node-bootstrap daemonset/job CrashLoopBackOff.
- kubelet logs: "rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed" when talking to container runtime.
- TLS handshake errors when pulling from private registry.

Commands run recently:
- kubectl get nodes -o wide  # shows new-node-abc NotReady
- kubectl describe node new-node-abc  # KubeletNotReady, CNI not ready events
- ssh ubuntu@<node> sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n200  # see kubelet runtime connection errors
- sudo journalctl -u containerd -n200  # sometimes connection closed / segfaults
- sudo crictl ps -a  # empty or backlog of initializing containers
- sudo ls -la /etc/cni/net.d  # sometimes empty when CNI not installed
- kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | grep new-node-abc  # kube-proxy pending, calico-node CrashLoopBackOff
- kubectl logs ds/calico-node -n kube-system -c calico-node --tail=200 --since=1h  # IPAM / kernel module hints

Helm steps tried:
- helm upgrade --install node-bootstrap ./charts/node-bootstrap -f values/staging.yaml --namespace kube-system --wait --timeout 10m  # sometimes job completes, sometimes ImagePullBackOff
- docker/crictl pull <private-reg>/node-bootstrap:sha123  # intermittent x509 errors

Error snippets saved:
- "rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed" (kubelet -> containerd)
- "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" (registry TLS)
- "CNI failed to set up pod network: no IP addresses available" (IPAM)
- "Failed to register node \"new-node-abc\": timeout waiting for the condition"

Hypotheses:
1) Registry CA issue: nodes sometimes missing custom CA, so image pulls fail and critical pods never start. Evidence: manual CA install fixes pull.
2) containerd intermittent crash / socket issues causing kubelet unable to start containers. Evidence: containerd logs show connection closed or crashes.
3) CNI ordering: CNI/Calico failing to initialize leads to NetworkUnavailable; /etc/cni/net.d missing on affected nodes.
4) kubelet flags/cloud-provider mismatch less likely but check systemd unit args.

Quick repro approach:
- Launch fresh instance from same AMI, run cloud-init manually, tail /var/log/cloud-init-output.log, journalctl -u containerd -f and kubelet -f to observe race conditions.

Collection checklist (runbook items):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
- kubectl describe node <node>
- ssh to node: sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n500 --no-pager | tail -n200
- sudo journalctl -u containerd -n500 --no-pager | tail -n200
- sudo crictl ps -a; sudo crictl logs <container-id>
- sudo ls -la /etc/cni/net.d && sudo cat /etc/cni/net.d/*
- sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init-output.log
- curl -vk https://<private-reg-host>/v2/  # registry TLS check

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Manually added CA cert to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/custom-reg.crt && update-ca-certificates && restart containerd => crictl pull succeeded.
- Added systemd drop-in to delay kubelet start by 60s to avoid cloud-init race (temporary).
- Tried larger instance types to rule out resource-induced containerd crashes.

Next steps / TODO:
- [ ] Add prebootstrap registry check in Helm chart (crictl pull) and write success marker before CNI/kubelet proceed.
- [ ] Make cloud-init idempotent for CA install + add retries.
- [ ] Consider gating node registration via register-node=false during bootstrap then register after checks.
- [ ] Collect full journald logs for three failing instances and attach to GH issue platform/infra#789.
- [ ] Audit AMIs and containerd/kernel versions across ASG.

On-incident quick commands to run:
- kubectl get events --all-namespaces --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n200
- kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | egrep "<node>|calico|kube-proxy|node-bootstrap"
- On node: sudo systemctl restart containerd && sudo systemctl restart kubelet && watch -n2 'journalctl -u kubelet -n50 --no-pager | tail -n20'

Random notes:
- Autoscaler may mark instance as healthy too early; consider making instance health depend on kubelet readiness.
- Gating registration by kubelet is invasive but would avoid scheduling on half-baked nodes.

Keep as scratch notes; draft runbook later if we want to formalize.

-- Marcus
